attacks.claim: A 4.7 schedule edit causes the cloud to discard the v2 (8-period) copy, so a later re-upgrade to 4.8 permanently loses periods the user built on 4.8, with no user warning and no restore path. The QA matrix tests only edit-on-4.8 then downgrade, never edit-on-4.7 then re-upgrade.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." / QA: "edit on 4.8, downgrade to 4.7 via OTA, schedule present and correct" (ABSENT: edit-on-4.7 then re-upgrade test; ABSENT: user notice before discard)

attacks.claim: The revert path is an operator action that irreversibly deletes user Home/Away history and switches off a user-enabled feature. The Rollback section lists no user notification or consent step, and does not say whether history can be preserved.
attacks.evidence: "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path; schedules fall back to their v1 copy and Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)."

attacks.claim: The downgrade projection from 8 periods to 4 uses a selection rule ('closest to anchors') with no defined tie-break, and the 'simplified' notice appears only in the app. Thermostat-only users on 4.7, or app users who never open the app, get a changed schedule with no indication of which periods were dropped.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors" / "The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods." (ABSENT: tie-break rule; ABSENT: on-device notice)

attacks.claim: Stage-1 gates are too small to be meaningful. At ~6,100 units, 0.05% is about 3 boot-revert events and the 0.1% page threshold is about 6 per 6 h. No minimum sample count, dwell time, or power basis is stated, so the advance and halt decisions are not statistically grounded.
attacks.evidence: "boot-revert rate < 0.05%" at "1% (~6,100)" / "exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window"

attacks.claim: Advance criteria are fleet-wide against an undefined 'baseline', yet sampling is stratified by rev and HVAC type. A regression confined to one hardware rev (e.g. rev C at 51% of fleet) or one HVAC type can be averaged out and pass every stage gate. No per-stratum criterion is given.
attacks.evidence: "Each stage is a random sample stratified by hardware rev and HVAC type." / "HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline"

attacks.claim: Behaviour is undefined when the revert install itself fails or is interrupted during the ~90 s window, while relays are held open. Auto-revert covers only boot and self-test failures of 4.8, not an incomplete 4.7 install.
attacks.evidence: "During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)." / "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically." (ABSENT: revert-install failure or interruption handling)

attacks.claim: Monitoring pages firmware on-call only for boot reverts and offline rate. Schedule-sync errors and Away Assist health appear only on a dashboard, and the 6 h page window does not match 3–4 day stages, so slow-developing failures in the new 4.8 paths can go unpaged through stage advancement.
attacks.evidence: "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline." / "schedule-sync errors" listed under Fleet dashboard only

attacks.claim: The 7-day deletion of Home/Away state is stated only for the cloud state. Retention of Home/Away events in the telemetry ingest pipeline (+0.4%), in backups, and in support access is not stated, and no deletion-job verification or device-removal/account-deletion behaviour is described.
attacks.evidence: "it is kept 7 days and then deleted." / "projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest." (ABSENT: telemetry and backup retention; ABSENT: device-removal and account-deletion behaviour)

attacks.claim: The QA evidence for the revert path is thin and unlabelled by revision: 300 qa-fleet units with no per-rev breakdown, and the 72 h HIL bench has no stated per-configuration sample size, so 'Pass' labels do not show what was exercised.
attacks.evidence: "Tested on 300 `qa-fleet` units." / "Pass, 0 relay faults over 72 h"

attacks.claim: The artifact does not state whether LGL-4471 covers Quebec (Law 25) and PIPEDA obligations for inferred occupancy data across the Canadian fleet, nor does it quote the updated notice text. French release notes do not mention the new data category.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)." / "Release notes (English and French) are published at stage 1"

attacks.claim: The 6% runtime claim is backed by a 412-home trial with legal review cited, but the artifact body does not state control design, dispersion, or whether the trial population matches the fleet's rev mix and climates. Confirm the linked page carries these before publication.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%." / "reviewed by legal for substantiation, LGL-4472"

attacks.claim: Away Assist applies user-set Away setpoints automatically, and the artifact states no floor or freeze-protection check for those setpoints. Impact is bounded because setpoints are user-chosen.
attacks.evidence: "Away uses the user's existing Away setpoints."

attacks.claim: Away Assist failure modes are unspecified: sensor fault or stuck state, and reboot or schedule-boundary behaviour of the 2 h timer. None are covered by QA beyond the basic on/off path.
attacks.evidence: "sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods" / QA: "on → Away after 2 h no motion, back on motion; off → history deleted"

attacks.claim: The 'always able to return to previous firmware' guarantee depends on the anti-rollback counter staying unchanged. Any future security release that bumps it strands 4.8 units. This is not a blocker here but needs a recorded release-policy constraint.
attacks.evidence: "4.8 does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter (no security fixes in this release), so 4.7 remains installable."

attacks.claim: 'Rolling out over the next two weeks' does not match stages totalling 11 days plus an open-ended stage 4 with no duration, and the stage gates have no timeout if telemetry is incomplete.
attacks.evidence: "Rolling out over the next two weeks." vs "3 days", "4 days", "4 days", "—"

attacks.claim: Assistive-technology testing covers the app 9.3 screens only. The 9.2 'Update the app' prompt, the schedule 'simplified' notice, and the on-device Away Assist disclosure have no VoiceOver, TalkBack, or 200% text checks.
attacks.evidence: "App 9.2 viewing an 8-period schedule shows update prompt, no edit | Pass" / "App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text | Pass"

attacks.claim: No signing-key rotation or revocation procedure is described for the Ed25519 image-signing key, which matters if 4.8 ever becomes the only path off a compromised 4.7.
attacks.evidence: "Images are signed (Ed25519); the bootloader verifies before swap" (ABSENT: key rotation and revocation procedure)

attacks.claim: Egress of ~1.5 TB assumes one download per unit. Retries, postponed-then-resumed downloads, and revert re-pushes are excluded, and the 'within the monthly commit' claim gives no commit size or headroom.
attacks.evidence: "2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract, within the monthly commit."
